Sattelite's attitude control model

The model was designed to check whether it is worthwhile to use VR to control the rotation of a satellite. To simplify the task, the rotation is performed in only one axis, but it still follows the same principles by which a satellite would rotate in space.

For this purpose, it was necessary to create a physical model, test more than one method of controlling the rotary motor, and create a paper thoroughly analyzing such an application of virtual reality.

Work on this topic as a whole became the subject of my master's thesis.

Status:

completed

Application type:

physical object control system

Technologies used:

Rpi.GPIO, pigpio, aiortc, WebRTC protocol, WebXR, Rasberry Pi 3B+

Programming languages:

Python, C, pigpio assembly, JavaScript

Main features:

  • control of the rotational position of the model without using an external arm
  • receiving and transmitting images with minimal delay
  • generation of an immersive image for playback in VR goggles based on data from a stereo camera
  • a range of tools for testing the behavior of created systems

Pygame snake

A spontaneous project that started as a quick, personal version of the Snake game and was then developed according to the motto "what else can I improve here."

It was an ideal place to experiment with object-oriented design paradigms, project structure, asynchronicity, and all networking-related issues such as: bandwidth, latency, message blocking on both the client and host side, as well as on intermediate devices invisible from the user's perspective.

Status:

further development planned

Application type:

network game

Technologies used:

pygame, asyncio, pydantic, fastapi, protobuf

Programming languages:

Python

Main features:

  • asynchronous handling of the main game loop and interactive menu
  • object-oriented approach to controlling game elements
  • configurable game settings, including control buttons
  • multiplayer using the host-client model

Python CProfile VSC Extension

An extension for VS Code that came in handy during another project. I couldn't find a free profiler that would conveniently show me where the bottlenecks in my application were, so I created my own.

However, there was no need to build the entire mechanism. After thoroughly checking available solutions, I found a program built into the Python language from which I could retrieve the necessary data. So I only wrote the extension that transforms this data into a convenient interface. This way, I gained the stability of a proven profiler and the convenience associated with a modern appearance.

Status:

completed

Application type:

application extension

Technologies used:

pstats, cprofile

Programming languages:

Python, TypeScript

Main features:

  • using cprofile via the VSCode interface
  • line coloring and displaying execution time for each function in the working folder

Sketchbook Krita Plugin

An extension for the Krita graphics editor, which I use regularly. Despite many useful existing features, it lacked the ability to create and save quick sketches without distractions in the form of the multi-step built-in export function.

The extension is meant to mimic the experience of using a real sketchbook, where the artist doesn't need to worry about what to name their work or where to put it, yet all their images remain organized according to the order they were created and bound together in a coherent form.

Such a solution significantly improves UX by drawing on the experiences of the average user, taken from real life.

Status:

completed

Application type:

application extension

Technologies used:

PyQt5

Programming languages:

Python

Main features:

  • automation of saving a document and opening a new one with a single button (or keyboard shortcut)
  • support for predefining the dimensions of a new document
  • PyQt interface for creating new document groups, called sketchbooks
